definition: The International Aerial Robotics Competition (IARC) is a university-based robotics competition held on the campus of the Georgia Institute of Technology, currently hosted by RoboNation.
details: Since 1991, collegiate teams with the backing of industry and government have fielded autonomous flying robots in an attempt to perform missions requiring robotic behaviors not previously exhibited by a flying machine. The term “aerial robotics” was coined by competition creator Robert Michelson in 1990 to describe a new class of small highly intelligent flying machines. Successive years of competition saw these aerial robots grow from vehicles that could barely maintain themselves in the air, to automatons which are self-stable, self-navigating, and able to interact with their environment. The goal of the competition has been to provide a reason for the state-of-the-art of aerial robotics to move forward. Challenges have been geared towards producing advances. From 1991 through 2009, six missions were proposed. Each involved fully autonomous robotic behavior undemonstrated at the time. In October 2013 a seventh mission was proposed. It was the first to involve interaction between aerial robots and multiple ground robots. explainer.lead: The International Aerial Robotics Competition is a university-based competition, held since 1991 and currently hosted by RoboNation, in which collegiate teams field autonomous flying robots. It matters because it pushes teams toward robotic behaviours not previously exhibited by flying machines.

tiers.eli5: It is a contest where student teams build flying robots that must complete missions on their own, no remote control.
tiers.practitioner: Teams backed by industry and government build autonomous aerial robots to perform competition missions. A pitfall is assuming the missions track today's hardware limits: successive years saw vehicles grow from barely staying airborne to far more capable behaviour.
tiers.paperLevel: The IARC has run since 1991 as a university-based competition on the Georgia Institute of Technology campus, currently hosted by RoboNation, with missions requiring robotic behaviours not previously exhibited by a flying machine; the term aerial robotics was coined by creator Robert Michelson in 1990.

explainer.example: A collegiate team enters an autonomous flying robot that must complete a mission without human control, a benchmark that has advanced from basic flight to complex robotic behaviour since 1991.
